info.title: Slate Core API
info.description: SLATE-203 scaffold contract. The tenant is always resolved server-side from the session principal, never from a client header alone (Master Plan Section 13). This is a stub committed so later phases can contract-test.

sessionCookie.name: slate_session
sessionCookie.description: Server-verified session. The scaffold adapter takes the principal from trusted session middleware.

TenantId.name: X-Tenant-Id
TenantId.description: Tenant the request acts on. Honored only when the session authorizes it; 403 otherwise. A session-bound active tenant wins and the header may only repeat it.

Setting.description: A tenant setting. `valueType` records the type the value was written with so `value` round-trips unchanged.

value.description: The stored value; its JSON type always agrees with `valueType`.

UpdateSettingRequest.description: Only `value` is accepted: the tenant comes from the resolved session context and `valueType` is derived from the value, so no client may supply either.

value.description: The value to store. `undefined` is not expressible in JSON, so omit the field is rejected rather than stored.

FeatureFlagMap.description: Server-authoritative flag map for the resolved tenant: `override -> registry default -> false`. Only flags declared in the code-owned registry appear, and an undeclared key always resolves to `false` rather than erroring.

UpdateFeatureFlagRequest.description: A boolean sets the tenant override and `null` clears it, so the tenant reverts to the registry default. A client never supplies a tenant id.

FeatureFlag.description: The resolved state of one flag after the write, not the raw stored override.

UnauthorizedTenantContext.description: 401 when no tenant can be resolved or the session is absent; 403 when the requested tenant is not authorized (no query is issued).

Forbidden.description: The authenticated actor lacks the required permission for the tenant.

Conflict.description: A unique constraint was violated (for example a duplicate email).

BadRequest.description: The request is not usable: a malformed body or unknown field, an invalid or over-long key, a value that cannot be stored, or an undeclared feature flag key. Rejected before any query or write.

ServerError.description: Unexpected failure; the request transaction is rolled back so no partial write survives.

get.summary: List the members of the resolved tenant
get.description: Requires the `users.read` permission in the resolved tenant. Rows are read through the tenant-scoped helper, so another tenant's members are not returned.

200.description: Members of the resolved tenant (at most 100).

post.summary: Provision an inactive user in the resolved tenant
post.description: Requires the `users.write` permission. The user, the tenant membership and exactly one attributed `audit_log` row commit in a single transaction before 201 is returned; `app.user.created` and `app.audit.recorded` are then published on the in-process bus.

201.description: The user was created and audited.

400.description: The body is not an object, carries unknown fields, or fails validation.

415.description: The Content-Type is not application/json (HTTP adapter).

get.summary: List the settings of the resolved tenant
get.description: Requires the `settings.read` permission in the resolved tenant. Rows are read through the tenant-scoped helper, so another tenant's settings are never returned. Nothing is cached: a committed change is visible on the next call.

200.description: Every setting of the resolved tenant, ordered by key.

put.summary: Upsert one setting in the resolved tenant
put.description: Requires the `settings.write` permission. The value's type is derived from the value itself, so it round-trips unchanged. The setting and exactly one attributed `audit_log` row commit in a single transaction before 200 is returned; `settings.updated` is then published on the in-process bus carrying the key only, never the value (Master Plan Section 61).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Dotted, namespaced setting key. URL-decoded, then validated: a malformed or over-long key is a 400 and no query is issued.

200.description: The setting was written and audited.

415.description: The Content-Type is not application/json (HTTP adapter).

get.summary: Resolve the feature flags of the resolved tenant
get.description: Requires the `features.read` permission. The map is computed server-side on every call as `tenant override -> registry default -> false`; a key nobody declared resolves to `false` and never errors (Master Plan Section 60). Flag definitions are code-owned, so adding one needs no migration.

200.description: The resolved flag map for the resolved tenant.

put.summary: Set or clear a feature flag override for the resolved tenant
put.description: Requires the `features.write` permission. `true`/`false` writes the tenant override and `null` clears it so the tenant reverts to the registry default. An undeclared key is a 400, so a client can never switch on behaviour nobody declared. The override and exactly one attributed `audit_log` row commit in a single transaction before 200 is returned; `feature.flag.updated` is then published carrying the key only, never the resolved state.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A key declared in the code-owned flag registry. URL-decoded; an undeclared key is a 400 and no query is issued.

200.description: The override was applied (or cleared) and audited.

415.description: The Content-Type is not application/json (HTTP adapter).
